JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed by the petitioner claiming compensation of .35,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the injuries sustained by the petitioner.

2. The petition averments in brief is that on 14.05.2019 at about 7.15 a.m., when he was travelling as a passenger in a Sea Bird Bus bearing Regn.No.KA-51-B-3090 driven by its driver by name Nayaz from Sira towards Bengaluru on NH-48 Road, when bus reached infront of India Overseas Bank,
Oorukere Village, Kasaba Hobli, Tumkuru, at that time the driver of Lorry bearing Sri.H.Nandish vs Sri.H.C.Nagarajaiah on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107005164/
2 Regn.No.KA-02-AF-3888 which was moving ahead of said Bus in a rash and negligent manner and applied sudden brake in middle of said road.

Due to which, petitioner and inmates of said bus sustained grievous injuries and immediately, he was shifted to District Hospital, Tumkuru, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and again he was shifted to BGS Global Institute of Medical Science & Hospital, Uttarahalli Main Road, Kengeri, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and spent .4,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and was working as a Packing wages in Export overseas and earning a sum of .13,875/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, he became permanent disablement.
The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of Lorry by its driver.
The respondents being the Insurers and owners of the offending vehicles are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
3. In spite of service of notice, respondent No.1, 3, 5 & 7 did not appear before the tribunal, hence they have been placed as ex-parte.
The respondent No.2, 4, 6 & 8 appeared before the tribunal through their respective counsels and filed their separate written statement.
4. The 2nd respondent in his written statement has contended that this claim petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to dismissed.

Further this respondent admitted the issuance of Commercial vehicle (Passenger Carrying) Package Policy in respect of Bus bearing Regn.No.KA-51-B-3090, but the original copy of policy is in possession and control of respondent No.1 and the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of policy.

Further contended that the driver of insured vehicle has no valid and effective driving license to drive the bus at the time of accident and also no permit to ply the vehicle in the place of accident.

Further contended that the accident in question was not occurred on account of rash and negligent driving of insured vehicle and said vehicle was driven by its driver very slowly and cautiously on the correct side of road.

Further contended that the unfortunate accident occurred only due to negligence driving of drivers of car bearing Regn.No.KA-04- MH-1186, Car bearing Regn.No.MH-12-MF-0272 and lorry bearing Regn.No.UP-70-GT-2486 and lorry bearing Regn.No.KA-02-AF-3888 and hence it is clear that the accident took place due to negligence of drivers of above vehicles.

Further contended that the owner and insurer of Car bearing Regn.No.KA-04-MB-1186 and Car bearing Regn.No.MH-12-MF- 0272 and Lorry bearing Regn.No.UP-70-GT-2486 are also necessary and proper parties to case.
The amount claimed by petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.
5. 4th

Respondent in his written statement has contended that the charge sheeted vehicle/offending vehicle Lorry bearing No.KA-02-AF-3888 was not having the valid insurance with this respondent on the date of alleged accident.

Further contended that the insurance Policy No.VGC0445120000100 and valid from 05.02.2019 to 04.02.2020 in respect of vehicle Lorry bearing Regn.No.KA-02- AF-3888, the aforesaid policy has issued with respect of vehicle Lorry bearing Regn.No.KA-02-AF-3888 for period from 05.02.2017 to 04.02.2018.

Further the third respondent issued the cheque bearing No.00024 dated: 04.02.2018 drawn on Kotak-Mahindra Bank, Chord Road, Vijayanagar Branch, Bengaluru for a sum of .63,012/- towards the premium for Sri.H.Nandish vs Sri.H.C.Nagarajaiah on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107005164/
3 the renewal of insurance policy.

Further the aforesaid cheque with a good faith this respondent issued the Policy No.VGC0445120000101 to be valid from 05.02.2018 to 04.02.2019 for the premium of .63,012/- to the vehicle bearing Regn.No.KA-02-AF-3888.
Further the aforesaid cheque was dishonoured as "Funds Insufficient".
Further this respondent issued notice of cancellation of policy.

Further contended that there is no valid and effective policy which was in force on 14.05.2019 i.e., the date of accident, in other words, when there is no policy which was issued to third respondent when no premium was received by this respondent.
Further the altered fake policy, the total premium is shown as .57,640/- which was actually charged for policy issued for the period of 05.02.2017 to 04.02.2018.
Further the premium charged for cancelled Policy No.VGC0445120000101 Was an enhanced amount of .63,012/- the payment of which was dishonored.
Further contended that the vehicle Lorry bearing No.KA-02-AF-3888 was not insured with this respondent on the date of alleged accident.

Further the policy particulars furnished by petitioner namely the Policy No.VGC0445120000100 was issued by this respondent in respect of vehicle Lorry bearing No.KA-02-AF- 3888 for the period of 05.02.2017 to 04.02.2018 and not for the period of 05.02.2019 to 04.02.2020 as stated in petition.
Further when there is no valid and effective policy which was in force on the date of alleged accident.
Further there is no policy which was issued by fourth respondent to the third respondent in respect of Lorry bearing No.KA-02-AF-3888, the claim against this respondent.

6. Further in the additional written statement of 4 th respondent contended that this respondent has not issued motor policy of insurance in favor of third respondent in respect of lorry bearing No.KA-02-AF-3888 covering the date of accident.
The policy number shown in petition that is VGC0445120000100 valid from 05.02.2019 to 04.02.2020 was not issued by this respondent in favor of third respondent in respect of lorry.

Further this respondent had issued policy in favor of third respondent in respect of lorry bearing No.KA-02- AF-3888 for a period from 05.02.2017 to 04.02.2018 under policy No.VGC0445120000100 and it was not valid as on the date of accident,
hence the petition against this respondent to be dismissed.
Further the lorry did not held valid insurance coverage as on the date of accident that is on 14.05.2019.

The third respondent get over the penalty/fine that my be levied by the police to non insured vehicle, tampered the period policy as 05.02.2019 to 04.02.2020 as against period 05.02.2017 to 04.02.2018 mentioned in original policy.
This clearly reveals the policy was fabricated.
Further contended that on the date of accident, the lorry was being driven in a reasonable speed and careful manner and there was no rashness or negligence on the part of driver of lorry.
The accident occurred due to negligence on the part of driver of bus in which petitioner was travelling.
The amount claimed by petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of petition.
7. The 6th respondent in his written statement has contended that the petitioner has filed the above claim petition U/s.166 of M.V.Act.
When the claim is U/s.166 of M.V.Act the petitioner has to plead and prove rash and negligence on the part of driver of vehicle said to have caused the alleged accident.
In the above claim petition there is no pleading that the alleged accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of lorry.
Further this respondent contended that there are several vehicles are implicated in the alleged accident.
Further contended that petitioner has not made the driver of lorry who alone can speak to cause of accident, a party to proceedings.

Further the alleged injuries said to have been suffered by petitioner are not due to any rash and negligent Sri.H.Nandish vs Sri.H.C.Nagarajaiah on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107005164/

There is no direct or indirect collision between the lorry and bus in which the petitioner was said to be travelling.
Further contended that the bus bearing No.KA-51-B-3090 in which the petitioner was said to be travelling.
The bus and lorry bearing No.UP-70-GT- 2486 were moving in opposite directions i.e., the bus was proceeding from Sira towards Bengaluru.
Whereas the lorry UP-70-GT-2486 was proceeding from Bengaluru towards Tumkuru.
The bus bearing No.KA-51-B-3090 was moving behind one lorry bearing No.KA-02-AF-3888, which was also proceeding from sira side to Bengaluru.

When the lorry suddenly applied brake and slow down, the driver of bus in which the petitioner was travelling driving the same in a rash and negligent manner,
without maintaining the safe distance from the vehicle moving ahead of it, had hit the lorry.
Due to which, the passengers in bus were said to be injured.
The amount claimed by petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prays for dismissal of petition.

8. Further the 8th respondent in his written statement has contended that the driver of vehicle Car bearing Regn.No.KA-04-MB-1186 was not holding a valid and effective driving license at the time of alleged accident.
Further contended that there is no nexus between the injured and the car.

Hence,
prays for dismissal of petition.

9. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following:
ISSUES 1.

Whether petitioner proves that, he sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 14.05.2019 at about 7.15 a.m., on NH-48, Over Bridge road, infront of Indian Overseas Bank, Oorukere Village, Kasaba Hobli, Tumakuru, when he was traveling in a Sea Bird Bus bearing Registration No.KA-51-B-3090, due to the rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing Registration No.KA-02-AF-3888 by its driver?
2. Whether the respondent No.4 proves that he has not issued valid policy with respect of lorry bearing Registration No.KA-02-AF-3888 as alleged in the written statement?
3. Whether the respondent No.4 further proves that policy No.VGC0445120000100 is created as alleged in the written statement?
4. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the claim petition?

If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
5.
What order or award?
10. In order to prove case of petitioner, petitioner examined himself as PW.1, Dr.Nagaraj.B.N examined as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.18 and closed his side of evidence.

On the other hand, the 4th respondent insurance company examined its State Head Legal as RW.1,
the Legal Manager in 2nd respondent insurance company examined as RW.2, the Legal Manager in 8 th respondent insurance company examined as RW.3 and the Administrative Officer in 6th Sri.H.Nandish vs Sri.H.C.Nagarajaiah on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107005164/
5
respondent insurance company examined as RW.4 and got marked documents at Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.15 and closed their side of evidence.
11. I have heard the arguments from both sides and perused the material available on record.
The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself stepped into the witness box and filed an affidavit in lieu of chief examination and examined as PW.1.
In his chief examination also he has deposed that due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Sea Bird Bus, the accident occurred.
Further in his cross examination, he has deposed that due to negligence of driver of Bus the accident occurred.
Further in his cross examination, he has admitted that police have filed charge sheet against the driver of sea bird Bus.
PW.1 in addition to his oral evidence, he has produced Ex.P.2 - first information lodged by one Sri.S.U.Naganagowdra, S/o.Ujjanagowda.

In his first information,
he has narrated the involvement of various vehicles in accident.
On the basis of first information lodged by Sri.S.U.Naganagowdra, the police registered the case as per Ex.P.1 against the drivers of all the vehicles involved in the accident.
After accident the police went near the place of accident and drew up Mahazar as per Ex.P.6 by narrating the place of accident.
Further the petitioner produced Ex.P.8 - IMV Report to show the damages caused to vehicles.
15. The respondent No.2 insurance company examined its Legal Manager as RW.2.

In his chief examination, he has deposed that the insured Bus bearing Regn.No.KA-51-B-3090 was driving slowly and carefully, at that time the drivers of vehicles Car bearing Regn.No.KA-04-MH-1186, Car bearing Regn.No.MH-12-MF-0272, Lorry bearing Regn.No.UP-70-GT- 2486, Lorry bearing Regn.No.KA-02-AF-3888 and KSRTC Bus careless driving of drivers of vehicles, the accident occurred.
There was no negligence on the part of driver of insured vehicle.

In his cross examination,
he has admitted that there was an accident between lorry and Bus.

The police after thorough investigation filed charge sheet as per Ex.P.5 against the drivers by name A1 - Sri.Manjunath.B.V,
S/o.Vishwanath Shetty.B.K - driver of Hundai Car bearing Regn.No.KA-04-MB- 1186, A2 - Sri.H.Nandish vs Sri.H.C.Nagarajaiah on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107005164/

6 Sri.Gafran Khan, S/o.Mukthar Ali - driver of Lorry bearing Regn.No.UP-70-GT-2486, A3 - Sri.Manjunath, S/o.Late Nagappa - driver of Lorry bearing Regn.No.KA-02-AF-3886, A4 - Sri.Nayaz, S/o.Mohammed Ali - driver of Sea Bird Private Bus bearing Regn.No.KA-51-B-3090.

Further on perusal of charge sheet, the police alleged that on the one side of road there was an accident between the car and Bus, at that time one lorry bearing Regn.No.UP-70-GT-2486 loaded with fish came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against Car bearing Regn.No.MH-12-MF-0272, as a result the fish fell on the road by seeing jumping of fish on road, the lorry bearing Regn.No.KA-02-AF-3888 came from on the other side of road stopped his Lorry without observing the vehicles coming his behind, as a result the driver of Sea Bird Bus bearing Regn.No.KA-51-B-3090 dashed to rare portion of lorry.
On perusal of charge sheet the accident occurred on two roads among different vehicle.

So, on meticulous perusal of charge sheet averments and evidence placed by both the parties there was no nexus between accident with respect of the other side vehicle involved in the accident with the Vehicle Lorry bearing Regn.No.KA-02-AF-3888 and vehicle Bus bearing Regn.No.KA-51-B-3090.
16.
But the learned counsel for respondent No.2 vehemently argued that due to negligent act of Lorry bearing Regn.No.UP-70-GT-2486, the accident occurred and he is liable to pay compensation.
The respondent No.2 did not place any materials before the tribunal to establish that due to negligence on the part of driver of Lorry bearing Regn.No.UP- 70-GT-2486 the accident occurred.
On perusal of evidence placed by both the parties there is no nexus between the Lorry bearing Regn.No.UP-70-GT-2486, Lorry bearing Regn.No.KA-02-AF-3888 and Bus bearing Regn.No.KA-51-B- 3090.

So, when the accident took place in different road and then there is no need to discuss negligence on the part of driver of KSRTC Bus bearing Regn.No.KA-63-F-0103, Car bearing Regn.No.KA-04-MB-1186 and Lorry bearing Regn.No.UP-70-GT-2486 in this case.

So, this tribunal not proceed to discuss negligence of the above said vehicles and only this tribunal considered the negligence between the Lorry bearing Regn.No.KA-02-AF-3888 and Bus bearing Regn.No.KA- 51-B-3090.
17.

As per charge sheet the driver of Lorry bearing Regn.No.KA-02-AF-3888 by seeing the jumping of fish on the other side of road he suddenly applied the brake, as a result the driver of Bus bearing Regn.No.KA-51-B-3090 dashed to rear portion of lorry.

So, it clearly indicates that the driver of lorry without observing the vehicles came to his behind he applied the brake, further it appears that the Bus which was coming behind the lorry without maintaining minimum distance from lorry, as a result the driver of Bus dashed the rear portion of lorry.

So, I am of the opinion that both the drivers of lorry and Bus have contributed their negligence towards the accident; as such this tribunal holds that both the drivers have contributed equal negligence towards the accident.
Hence, I answered Issue No.1 Partly in the Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:-
The respondent No.4 Insurance Company filed an objections by contending that the Lorry bearing Regn.No.KA-02-AF-3888 was not insured with this respondent.

The policy particulars furnished by petitioner namely Policy No.VGC0445120000100 was issued by this respondent in respect of Lorry bearing Regn.No.KA-02-AF-3888 for a period from 05.02.2017 to 04.02.2018.

In order to prove the contention of respondent No.4 Insurance Company examined its Sri.H.Nandish vs Sri.H.C.Nagarajaiah on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107005164/
7
State Head Legal by name Sri.Sudhakara.H
as RW.1.

In his chief examination also he has deposed that fourth respondent issued policy in favour of 3 rd respondent in respect of Lorry bearing Regn.No.KA-02-AF-3888 for a period from 05.02.2017 to 04.02.2018 under Policy No.VGC0445120000100.
Even in his cross examination also deposed that they have issued policy to lorry bearing Regn.No.KA-02-AF-3888 for a period from 05.02.2017 to 04.02.2018.

The respondent No.4 produced Ex.R.2 - Copy of Insurance Policy bearing No.VGC0445120000100 and from 05.02.2017 to 04.02.2018.
19.
The respondent No.3 owner of Lorry did not appear before the tribunal to prove that his lorry duly insured with 4 th respondent.
Neither petitioner nor 3rd respondent produced copy of policy to show that the lorry insured with 4 th respondent at the time of accident.
The owner of vehicle not rebutted the evidence placed by insurance company.
The 4 th respondent insurance company specifically contended that they have not issued the policy with respect of lorry bearing Regn.No.KA-02-AF-3888 at the time of accident.
So, the materials placed by 4th respondent insurance company clearly shows that the 4th respondent insurance company not issued policy to lorry bearing Regn.No.KA-02-AF-3888 at the time of accident.
Hence, I answered Issue No.2 in the Affirmative.
20. Issue No.3:- In view of answering issue No.2 in the Affirmative, the Issue No.3 does not survive for consideration.
21. Issue No.4:
In view of held issue No.1 in the Affirmative, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

To assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury,
pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance, loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc., let me discussion one by one.
(i) Towards injury and pain and suffering:- The petitioner contended that due to accident he sustained injuries and underwent surgery and later discharged with an advice to take follow up treatment.

In order to prove the injuries caused to him,
petitioner has produced wound certificate issued by District Hospital, Tumakuru marked at Ex.P.7, wherein it discloses that the injury No.1 is simple in nature and injury No.2 to 4 are grievous in nature.

So, on perusal of records he took treatment in hospital as an inpatient and the petitioner examined Dr.Nagaraj.B.N examined as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.14 & 15.
PW.2/doctor has deposed that he examined the petitioner for assessment of permanent physical disability and he assessed disability for right lower limb at 51%, for left lower limb at 51% and to left upper limb at 39% and to the whole body at 33%.
By considering the injuries and facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal is of the view that the compensation of .55,000/- is just and reasonable towards pain and suffering.
(ii) Towards Medical Expenses:
The petitioner has claimed compensation towards medical expenses.
The petitioner contended that he took treatment at Hospital.

The petitioner has produced Sri.H.Nandish vs Sri.H.C.Nagarajaiah on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107005164/
8
75 medical bills for .1,28,654/- marked at Ex.P.10 and 24 medical bills for .59,900/- marked at Ex.P.16, 45 medical prescriptions marked at Ex.P.11 and 11 medical prescriptions marked at Ex.P.17.
The respondents not rebutted the other medical bills by placing cogent evidence.
So, Tribunal is of the view that compensation of .1,88,554/- is just and reasonable towards medical expenses.
(iii) Towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant charges:
On perusal of records, the accident occurred on 14.05.2019 and the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient in the hospital.
On perusal of evidence, the petitioner was inpatient at Hospital as he has sustained injuries.

So,
during the time of treatment the petitioner also required good food and extra nourishment.

The petitioner has produced Discharge Summaries marked at Ex.P.3, 4 & 18, issued by BGS Global Institute of Medical Sciences & Hospital and District Hospital, Tumakuru, wherein it shows that petitioner has taken treatment from 01.07.2019 to 20.07.2019, 14.05.2019 to 02.06.2019 and again from 13.07.2021 to 29.07.2021 i.e., for a period of 55 days.

sentences.text: Considering the said facts, the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of .400/- per day for 55 days to a sum of .22,000/- is just and reasonable towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant.

(iv) Towards Conveyance:
The petitioner is the resident of Anchibarihatti Village, Lakkihalli Post, Hosadurga Tq, Chitradurga District and accident occurred on Infront of Indian Overseas Bank,
Over bridge, NH-48 Road, Oorukere Village, Kasaba Hobli, Tumkur, he has admitted for treatment at Hospital.
In order to prove this aspect the petitioner has produced discharge summaries.
Considering the injuries and facts of the case, the tribunal is of view that the compensation of .10,000/- is just and proper towards conveyance charges.
(v) Towards loss of income during treatment:

The petitioner has contended that he was working as a Packing Wages in Export Overseas and earning a sum of .13,875/-
per month.
In order to prove his income, the petitioner has not produced any documents to show that he was earning .13,875/- per month.
In the absence of positive documents regarding his occupation and income, this tribunal will consider notional income.
Due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner might have not attended his regular work at least for a period of 2 months.
The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka fixed notional income of the year 2019 at .14,000/- per month for determination of income before Lok Adalat.

So, in view of fixing of notional income by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, it is just and proper to the Tribunal to follow the notional income as fixed by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka to decide the cases before this Tribunal also.
Case on hand the petitioner has not produced any relevant document to prove his income.
Accordingly, the notional income of petitioner during the year 2019 treated as .14,000/- per month as fixed by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for .28,000/- (14,000/- x 2) towards loss of income during treatment.

(vi) Towards Permanent Disability:
Sri.H.Nandish vs Sri.H.C.Nagarajaiah on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107005164/
9
The petitioner has contended that due to accident, he was inpatient at hospital, and sustained permanent disablement.
The petitioner also examined Dr.Nagaraj.B.N working as Orthopaedic Surgeon at SOADS and examined as PW.2.
PW.2/Doctor examined the patient clinically and radiologically to assess disabilities.

The doctor deposed that petitioner has sustained comminuted supracondylar fracture of right femur, comminuted proximal condyle fracture of left tibia and fracture of left humerus fracture and underwent ORIF with plate and screws for right supracondylar fracture of femur and ORIF with IMIL Nailing for left tibia on 14.05.2019 and ORIF with plate and screws for left humerus.

The doctor has examined the petitioner for assessment of disability and assessed the disability for right lower limb at 51% and left lower limb at 51% and for left upper limb at 39% and to the whole body at 33%.

In order to prove the disability, doctor has produced Ex.P.14 & 15 documents i.e.,
clinical notes and 3 X-ray films.
By considering the oral and documentary evidence and facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that the petitioner can do his work with difficulty.

Therefore,
considering all these aspects, the functional disability is assessed at 22%.

In order to prove age of the petitioner, he has produced Ex.P.12 - Notarized copy of Aadhaar Card, wherein the date of birth mentioned as 01.07.1981, the accident occurred on 14.05.2019, so the age of petitioner was 38 years as on the date of accident.
Hence, the same is taken into consideration for applying multiplier and multiplier '15' is applicable as per Smt. Sarla Verma case.

As per ratio laid down by Hon'ble supreme court in Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay kumar and another,
this tribunal not deducted personal expenses of petitioner out of his gross income.

entities.text: Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay kumar and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hence, future earning capacity of the petitioner due to permanent disability works out as under :
Annual Income before accident : (.14,000/- x 12) = .1,68,000/- Loss of future earning p.a. (22% of prior annual income) .36,960/-.
Multiplier applicable with reference to age - 15 Loss of future earnings - (.36,960/- x 15) = .5,54,400/-.
The petitioner is entitled for .5,54,400/- under the head of loss of future earning capacity.
(vii) Deprivation of Future Amenities:- The doctor has opined that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries and he is unable to do his day-today activities as earlier.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal is of the view that compensation of .20,000/- is just and reasonable under the head deprivation of future amenities.

(viii) Towards Future Medical Expenses:

The doctor/PW.2 has opined that the petitioner needs another surgery for removal of implants, the estimate of surgery is around .60,000/-.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case .30,000/- is just and reasonable under the head deprivation of future medical expenses.
